findings.passage: Two participants said his team privately lobbied the pope's advisers. Anthropic declined to discuss the private conversations.
findings.problem: An anonymously sourced report of private lobbying, with Anthropic declining comment, is an unresolved matter and a contested allegation. It is missing from the claim inventory (C41 stops at the organizer quote). The next sentence, 'A person familiar with his thinking told the Times...', is also uninventoried. C41 itself is marked class 'disputed' but durability 'stable' with an empty review_trigger. The page cannot be maintained if a correction, an on-record response from Olah or Anthropic, or follow-up reporting changes the account.
findings.acceptance_test: The evidence record has a claim for the lobbying passage and one for the 'person familiar with his thinking' passage, each citing S13 (the NYT/SLTrib feature). Those claims and C41 are marked durability 'unresolved', each with a concrete review_trigger, e.g. 'Re-check if Olah or Anthropic comments on the record, the NYT issues a correction, or new reporting on the Magnifica humanitas launch appears; otherwise re-check by 2027-05-25.' The prose keeps the attribution to anonymous participants and the declined comment.

findings.passage: Fortune, citing the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, put his net worth at just under $8 billion in June 2026. The figure depends on Anthropic's valuation and changes with it.
findings.problem: The time-sensitive claims (C23 net worth; C61/C63 role) are dated in prose. But their review triggers depend on 'after Anthropic's IPO prices', an event that has no date, is not mentioned in the article, and may never happen. Five years out, nothing in the record forces a re-check of the page's most perishable facts. Net worth is the fastest to go stale and is also a search-facing FAQ.
findings.acceptance_test: Each of C23, C61 and C63 has a review_trigger with a calendar fallback as well as event conditions, e.g. 'Re-check on any Anthropic IPO, a funding round that changes the valuation, or an announced role change, and in any case by 2027-06-01.' The net-worth FAQ keeps 'June 2026' and its source attribution in the same sentence as the figure.

findings.passage: That teenager is now one of the co-founders of Anthropic, the company behind Claude, where he leads the team trying to understand what actually happens inside AI models.
findings.problem: Co-founder status is permanent, but 'now ... where he leads the team' is an undated present-tense role claim in the introduction. The 'Who is Chris Olah?' FAQ ('where he leads interpretability research') repeats it. If his role changes, both the opening and the FAQ become wrong, with no date to show when they were true.
findings.acceptance_test: The permanent fact is separated from the changeable one, e.g. 'In 2021 he co-founded Anthropic, the company behind Claude, where as of 2026 he leads the team...'. The FAQ's role clause carries the same 'as of 2026' anchor or an equivalent date. C61 and C63 passages match the revised wording.

findings.passage: When the G20 summit came to Toronto, police raided the home of a man from HackLab
findings.problem: The hook is the most durable anchor in the article but carries no year. The court support and the 'year off' then float relative to other dated events (the 2012 Thiel Fellowship, 2013 Nielsen seminars). The standard requires absolute dates. The 80,000 Hours transcript (S01) gives the sequence: 'he was under house arrest for one year, and in the second year I took a year off university.' The Toronto G20 summit was in June 2010.
findings.acceptance_test: The opening sentence or paragraph dates the summit (June 2010). The year off is placed in absolute terms consistent with S01, e.g. 'the following year' or 2011–12. No new precision is added beyond what S01 and public summit dates support.

findings.passage: Days before Pope Leo XIV presented his encyclical on AI in May 2026, Olah read an advance copy.
findings.problem: The encyclical is unnamed in the body and the FAQ, which makes the passage harder to look up years from now. The cited Anthropic page names it ('Magnifica humanitas') and shows dateModified 2026-09-28, four months after the speech on 2026-05-25. So the quoted remarks sit on a page that has been edited since delivery, and the record does not note this.
findings.acceptance_test: The body (and the 'Who is Chris Olah?' FAQ if it mentions the encyclical) names 'Magnifica humanitas' once. The source entry for the Anthropic remarks records the page's modification date. C40 has a review_trigger to re-verify the quoted wording if the page changes again.

findings.passage: He is no longer single, he notes at the top, but he left the doc up "since it was an important document for me."
findings.problem: Relationship status is stated in the present tense on the authority of an undated note on a living page ('This profile was published in August 2022; I'm no longer single...'). C39's trigger, 'Re-check before any refresh; omit unless Olah publicly updates it', is not an actionable condition. If the note changes or the doc comes down, the sentence goes stale silently.
findings.acceptance_test: The prose describes the document, not his current status, e.g. 'A note later added to the top says he is no longer single...'. C39 has an observable trigger, e.g. 'Re-check if the note at colah.github.io/personal/dating/ changes or the page is removed; check at each refresh.' No speculation about a partner is added.

findings.passage: (9takes reads his fellow co-founder [Dario Amodei](/personality-analysis/dario-amodei) as a Six.)
findings.problem: This sentence depends on another page's current typing (Dario-Amodei is published as Type 6 today). That page is a separate living analysis. If it is retyped on refresh, this page contradicts it, and no claim or trigger links the two.
findings.acceptance_test: Either the parenthetical is cut, keeping the link to the Amodei page without stating its type, or the evidence record has a claim for it with review_trigger 'Re-check if the Dario Amodei page's enneagram value changes.'

findings.passage: In a [January 2021 thread](https://twitter.com/ch402/status/1348498446211112961) on why fantasy moves people
findings.problem: The thesis-bearing personal evidence (C28–C30, C35 and the 2020 neuron thread) rests on X/Twitter status links, a living personal page that has already been edited (the dating doc), and a syndicated copy of a paywalled NYT feature. All return 200 today. Over five years, these are the links most likely to disappear, and they would take the Four case's best evidence with them.
findings.acceptance_test: For each X thread, the dating doc and the SLTrib syndication, the evidence source records an archived URL (e.g. web.archive.org snapshot) or a saved excerpt location, alongside the live URL. The in-article links can stay as they are.

assessment: Five-year test: largely passes. The thesis (absence is met with publicized longing and a search for meaning, not a search for security) rests on 2010–2024 material across contexts: the court support, the Gilead and family threads, the dating doc, a decade of 'beauty' and 'sad' language. Removing the May 2026 Vatican episode leaves it intact, and the draft says so. The hook is a 2010 story, not this year's news. The weaknesses are in maintenance, not in the argument. (1) The sensitive, anonymously sourced Vatican lobbying and withdrawal reports are uninventoried or marked stable with no trigger (future-01). (2) Every time-sensitive trigger hangs on an undated Anthropic IPO (future-02). (3) Several present-tense or undated anchors (current role, the G20 year, the relationship note, the unnamed encyclical, a cross-page type claim) will drift. (4) The best personal evidence sits on easily lost X links. None of these weakens the type argument; all are cheap fixes to the evidence record and a few sentences of prose. Similarity advisory tripped on 'whose core emotion is shame' (Mike Faist) and 'the three types' (Hunter Schafer). These are ordinary triad vocabulary in one orientation sentence, not reused argument; the Olah-specific discriminator and evidence are distinct, so no finding is raised.
